linkedin.text:
The destination isn't the backdrop. It's the first slide of your presentation.

I've seen this play out across 130+ destinations over 16 years: when the location is unexpected, the content lands differently. People are more present. The conversations go deeper. The decisions that get made in those rooms tend to stick.

We had a client running an annual leadership summit — same content, different country. The shift in location alone changed how the executive team engaged with the material. They told us afterward it was the most productive version of the summit they'd run.

For senior decision-makers planning a conference, incentive trip or retreat: how much weight does your team actually put on the destination itself when you're building the brief?

Genuinely curious — comment below or DM me directly.

instagram.text:
The destination IS the message. 📍

When your people step off the plane somewhere genuinely unexpected, the event has already started — before the welcome dinner, before the keynote, before anything on the agenda.

We've produced events across 130+ destinations worldwide. The locations that land hardest are never the obvious ones.

Where's your next team experience taking place? Tell us in the comments — we might have stories from exactly that corner of the world. 👇

facebook.text:
Some venues just do the talking for you.

When your team lands somewhere genuinely unexpected — a cliffside retreat, a working vineyard, a city that still feels undiscovered — the energy in the room changes before the first agenda item is even read.

Across 130+ destinations, we've watched that moment happen thousands of times. The right place doesn't just host your event. It sets the whole tone for what you're trying to say as a business.

Planning something for your team and not sure where in the world to hold it? Drop the country or region you're considering in the comments — happy to share what we've seen work there.
